input: Draft a rental agreement for my spare room

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is a simple lodger licence or a full tenancy agreement changes the entire legal structure and clauses needed.
The number of tenants, whether they are known to the user, and any special circumstances (e.g. student, professional) affects how the agreement is tailored.
The country and region determines which landlord-tenant laws, deposit rules, and mandatory clauses apply — a UK agreement differs entirely from a US one.
The rent amount, deposit size, lease duration, and notice period are core terms that must be specified in the document.
What is included in the rent (utilities, Wi-Fi, parking, etc.) directly shapes the financial and responsibility clauses.
House rules (guests, pets, smoking, shared spaces) reflect the landlord's priorities and must be embedded as enforceable clauses.
Whether the user needs a legally watertight professional document or a clear, plain-English draft determines the tone, depth, and whether a lawyer review note is needed.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a spare room rental agreement
gold.taskDescription: Write a rental agreement document for the user's spare room to be used with a tenant.

questions.title: Which country and region is the property located in?
questions.description: The applicable landlord-tenant laws, required disclosures, and deposit rules vary significantly by jurisdiction (e.g. England, California, Ontario).

questions.title: Is this a lodger arrangement or a standalone tenancy?
questions.description: A lodger (who shares the home with the landlord) requires a licence agreement, while a sole-occupancy tenant requires a formal tenancy agreement — these are legally distinct documents.

questions.title: How many tenants, and do you already know who they are?
questions.description: The number of named tenants and whether they are identified yet affects how parties are described and whether joint-liability clauses are needed.

questions.title: What are the rent, deposit amount, and lease duration?
questions.description: These are the core financial and time-bound terms that anchor the entire agreement.

questions.title: What is included in the rent — utilities, Wi-Fi, parking?
questions.description: Clarifying what is and is not covered prevents disputes and shapes the bills and responsibilities clauses.

questions.title: What house rules matter most to you — pets, guests, smoking?
questions.description: The landlord's key restrictions and expectations need to be written into enforceable clauses within the agreement.

questions.title: Do you need a legally rigorous draft or a clear plain-English version?
questions.description: This determines the formality, depth of legal language, and whether a disclaimer advising professional legal review should be included.
